title: Elephant Yam (Suran): modeled ₹359/qtl left, Perumbavoor → Pampady
summary: August 2021: reported elephant Yam (Suran) prices at Perumbavoor and Pampady imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 89% of 19 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹359 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 22 same-variety market pairs screened for elephant Yam (Suran) in August 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Pampady report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: August 2021
scenes.caption: Perumbavoor (Kerala) and Pampady (Kerala) both reported elephant Yam (Suran) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 19 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Perumbavoor reported a median ₹2,200 per quintal. Pampady reported a median ₹2,700 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹500/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹500 per quintal, and Pampady was dearer on 89% of days.

scenes.headline: 76 km by road
scenes.caption: 76 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹16/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹224 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹83 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Pampady report, the rule selects 16 of 19 modeled shipping days. 14 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹359 per quintal (₹208 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Elephant Yam (Suran) route from Perumbavoor to Pampady was positive on 89% of matched days in August 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹35,900, or ₹20,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to elephant Yam (Suran)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹16/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Elephant Yam (Suran) route from Perumbavoor to Pampady was positive on 89% of matched days in August 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹35,900, or ₹20,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
